text: By this test Shakespeare had already been tried. A century and a half had gone by since the plays were first acted. In that interval the language and the customs of the stage had both changed; the taste of readers, besides, had been reformed more than once by critics who found much in him to censure. Yet the plays kept their place upon the stage and in the closet, and their hold upon the public had grown rather than weakened. Johnson put the matter in a single figure: "The stream of time, which is continually washing the dissoluble fabricks of other poets, passes without injury by the adamant of Shakespeare." (Johnson 1765)
